_comment: ADR 0044/0045 — common physics body templates. Per-game entity defs spread these via $extends to get sensible defaults. Override individual fields after the $extends to customize. Bits 1..16 from @lib.physics.layers used here; games with custom layer names can override collision_layer / collision_mask. ADR 0045: `body_type: "character"` creates a CharacterBody3D Node (move_and_slide-driven, the right pick for velocity-controlled actors). Other body_types create raw PhysicsServer3D RIDs.
_sizing_convention: Character template capsule dimensions come from a PRIMITIVE .glb under data/lib/assets/meshes/ — NOT from manual radius/height numbers. The engine reads the primitive's bbox at build time (physics_body_builder._glb_bbox) and fits the CapsuleShape3D: radius = max(bbox.x, bbox.z)/2, height = bbox.y. state.scale on the entity propagates uniformly to the body so the capsule and the visible mesh stay aligned. To change humanoid proportions: regenerate the primitive .glb (tools/gen_primitive_cylinder.py — adjust radius/height there). Never author radius/height in a per-entity collision_shape — that's the escape hatch pattern banned by .claude/rules/data-demo.md.

standard_character_player._comment: ADR 0045 — player CharacterBody3D. Capsule dimensions derived from primitive_humanoid_capsule.glb (bbox 0.30 × 1.0 × 0.30 → radius 0.15, height 1.0). state.scale brings it to final size (player at scale=1.7 → 0.255m radius × 1.7m tall — thin human silhouette).

standard_character_npc._comment: ADR 0045 — NPC CharacterBody3D. Same humanoid capsule primitive as the player; differs only in collision layer/mask.

standard_character_animal._comment: ADR 0045 — animal CharacterBody3D. Reuses the humanoid capsule primitive — works because quadrupeds happen to fit a tall thin capsule when bbox-derived from a normalized 1m-tall Tripo3D mesh + state.scale (rabbit=0.35, deer=1.6, wolf=1.0). If a specific animal needs different proportions, add another primitive .glb to lib/assets/meshes/ and reference it here — DON'T author manual radius/height.

static_decoration_no_collision._comment: For visible-but-non-blocking decoration. No body = no physics overhead. Use this template by NOT declaring a physics block on the entity.

rigid_projectile._comment: RigidBody3D projectile — Godot's PhysicsServer integrates it with the full 3D velocity vector (so a pitch-aimed shot rises/falls correctly) and gravity_scale 0 keeps it straight. CAVEAT: rigid bodies only move under a LIVE physics server; the headless scenario/step harness has none (it integrates only CharacterBody3D via tick_headless), so rigid projectiles are FROZEN in scenario tests — gate a projectile's hit RULE by placing the target within contact range (position-based), not by relying on headless flight.

character_projectile._comment: CharacterBody3D projectile — the only Yume body that moves VISIBLY (move_and_slide writes global_position back to state.position live; tick_headless does the same in scenario tests). Rigid bodies fly in PhysicsServer space but never write back to state, so they render frozen. Small sphere; collision_mask = wall only (stops at walls, passes THROUGH monsters — a contact RULE applies damage). LIMITATION: the character runner owns velocity.y (gravity/jump channel), so the projectile flies FLAT regardless of pitch — fine for ground targets, wrong for arc/vertical shots. A free-3D-velocity projectile (rigid + a body→state readback) is future work. Author the def with state_init.gravity 0. Used by doomarena3d bullets.

_authoring_note: Templates use $extends syntax: "physics": {"$extends": "@lib.physics.bodies.standard_character_animal"}. State.scale on the entity automatically propagates to the body's transform — author ONE template per archetype, vary instances via state.scale. Custom dimensions per def are an anti-pattern (see .claude/rules/data-demo.md § no escape hatches): if the lib value is wrong for an archetype, fix the lib.
